title: Hosted API: Harden request retry protection and escalation playbook for 5xx/timeouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: High-rate customer escalations surfaced a pattern of Hosted API 5xx errors and timeouts that amplified due to aggressive client-side retry logic. The cascade appears most pronounced under medium burst traffic where KV cache eviction and transient transformer memory pressure coincide with repeated retries. This ticket is the engineering playbook and targeted bugfix to stop the current escalations, prevent recurrence, and provide a verification path for impacted customers.

Scope: Hosted API front-end + runtime gateway behavior. We will validate no Dedicated or Private control planes require immediate code changes; however, the guidance and optional runtime toggles will be documented for Dedicated/Private customers.

Goals: 1) Provide immediate mitigation steps to stop error amplification and restore SLOs for impacted tenants. 2) Deploy a short-term code fix (retry coalescing + gateway backpressure) with minimal risk and fast rollback. 3) Add long-term protections (per-tenant in-flight limits, smarter KV-cache eviction backoff, and adaptive retry headers) and monitoring/alerts.

Proposed short-term actions (<= 24h): - Deploy gateway-level retry coalescing that collapses identical in-flight identical requests for 5s windows for same tenant+route. - Add a per-tenant in-flight request soft-limit (default 200) that returns 429 instead of letting retries flood backend. - Temporarily bump hosted-api request timeout for large customers from 30s to 45s where root cause shows occasional long-generation tails. - Blacklist the top 2 clients that repeatedly exceeded recommended retry behavior (contact SEs for names) and throttle to protect others.

Proposed medium-term fixes (2–3 sprints): - Implement adaptive retry-throttling using moving-window headroom and token-bucket per-tenant. - Address KV cache eviction race: add jittered refill delays and reduce worst-case eviction churn when facing heavy prefix-evictions. - Improve kernel scheduling fallbacks to reduce OOM-caused 5xx during sequence spikes. - Add explicit guidance and SDK headers to signal client retry policies (Retry-After, idempotency keys).

Monitoring & verification: - New Dashboards: hosted_api/5xx_by_route, hosted_api/retry_fanout_heatmap, tenant_inflight_counts. - Automated canary that simulates burst with exponential backoff clients and asserts error rate < 1% at 95th percentile. - Post-deploy smoke: run simulated load for 10 minutes then escalate if any 5xx > 0.5% for that window.

Rollout plan: 1) Patch and deploy gateway change to canary subset of regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). 2) Observe 30m, validate with simulated traffic and customer telemetry. 3) Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 hours if stable. 4) If regressions detected, rollback gateway change and enable temporary tenant-level throttles.

Communications: - Notify affected customers via status page and targeted emails (SE + CSM) with mitigations and ETA. - Internal: runbook update in Confluence and Slack #incident-ops thread pinned updates.

acceptance_criteria: Deployed gateway coalescing and per-tenant soft-limits in hosted regions with canary then full rollout.
5xx rate for affected tenants reduced to < 0.5% within 30 minutes of mitigation on production traffic.
Automated canary test reproducing burst + client retries passes (error rate < 1% at 95th).
Runbook and SDK guidance updated and communicated to SE/Support teams.
Follow-up tickets created for medium-term fixes (adaptive throttling, KV cache changes).
